paragraphs.zh: (54) Bezeichnung: BENZOYLCYCLOHEXANDIONE, VERFAHREN ZU IHRER HERSTELLUNG UND IHRE VERWENDUNG ALS HERBIZIDE UND PFLANZENWACHSTUMSREGULATOREN
paragraphs.en: (54) Title: BENZOYLCYCLOHEXANEDIONES, PROCESS FOR THEIR PREPARATION AND THEIR USE AS HERBICIDES AND PLANT GROWTH REGULATORS

paragraphs.zh: (57) Abstract The invention relates to benzocyclohexandiones of general formula (I), a method for the production and use thereof as herbicides and plant growth regulators. In said general formula (I), R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6 and R7 represent various radicals, L is an alkylene chain and Y and Z are a monoatomic bridging element.
paragraphs.en: (57) Abstract The invention relates to benzocyclohexandiones of general formula (I), a method for the production and use thereof as herbicides and plant growth regulators. In said general formula (I), R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6 and R7 represent various radicals, L is an alkylene chain and Y and Z are a monoatomic bridging element.
paragraphs.notes: Printed in English on the original page, so zh and en carry the same string. The radical indices 1 to 7 are printed as superscripts on R and are written inline here. Note the word benzocyclohexandiones as printed: it lacks the oyl that both title fields and the German abstract carry (Benzoylcyclohexandione). Transcribed as printed, not corrected; see discrepancies.

paragraphs.zh: (57) Zusammenfassung Es werden Benzoylcyclohexandione der allgemeinen Formel (I), Verfahren zu ihrer Herstellung und ihre Verwendung als Herbizide und Pflanzenwachstumsregulatoren beschrieben. In dieser allgemeinen Formel (I) stehen R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6 und R7 für verschiedene Reste, L für eine Alkylenkette, Y und Z für ein einatomiges Brückenelement.
paragraphs.en: (57) Abstract Benzoylcyclohexanediones of the general formula (I), processes for their preparation and their use as herbicides and plant growth regulators are described. In this general formula (I), R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6 and R7 stand for various radicals, L for an alkylene chain, Y and Z for a monoatomic bridging element.
paragraphs.notes: The radical indices 1 to 7 are printed as superscripts on R and are written inline here.

structures.position_in_drawing: 1st and only, centred in the lower half of the page, labelled (I) to its right
structures.core: Two rings joined by a carbonyl bridge. Left ring: a six-membered ring drawn as C(R6)=C(-C(=O)Ar) - C(=O) - Y - Z - (CH2)v - back to the R6 carbon, that is a cyclohexane-1,3-dione type ring in which two of the ring positions are drawn as the labelled atoms Y and Z, and in which a bracket ( )v encloses one CH2 ring vertex between Z and the R6-bearing carbon. Right ring: a benzene ring, drawn with three inner double bonds, attached to the bridging carbonyl.
substituents: left ring: R6 on the top ring vertex, the carbon that carries the ring C=C double bond
left ring: the aroyl bridge C(=O)-aryl on the ring carbon double bonded to the R6 carbon
left ring: =O (ketone) on the ring carbon between the aroyl-bearing carbon and Y
left ring: ring position labelled Y, drawn adjacent to the ring ketone carbon on one side and to Z on the other
left ring: ring position labelled Z, drawn adjacent to Y on one side and to the bracketed ( )v CH2 vertex on the other
left ring: (R7)w on a floating bond that is drawn from the label up and to the right, crossing the Z-Y bond; the attachment atom is unclear because the drawing deliberately does not fix it
benzene ring, numbering the attachment carbon as C1 and running towards R2: bridging C(=O) at C1
L-R1 at C3, that is a bond from the ring to L and a further bond from L to R1

drawings.notes: This is the Markush general formula (I) of the invention, printed on the PCT front page between the title block and the abstract block. It is a single generic structure, not a reaction scheme, so arrows is empty and presented_as invention_route means only that it is the invention's own subject matter and is not prior art. name and smiles are null because R1 to R7, L, Y, Z, v and w are all undefined variables on this page; no SMILES can be written without inventing atoms. The benzene locants C1 to C6 above are a reading convention for this record, taken by walking the drawn hexagon from the attachment carbon towards R2; the page prints no locants. Structure confidence is medium rather than high for one reason only: the (R7)w bond is a floating bond whose ring attachment point the drawing does not fix. Every drawn line and label is otherwise sharp and legible.

discrepancies.what: The printed English abstract calls the compounds benzocyclohexandiones, but the drawn formula (I) shows an aroyl group joining the two rings, which is a benzoylcyclohexanedione, and both title fields and the German abstract say Benzoyl.
discrepancies.drawing_says: formula (I) draws a substituted benzene ring joined by a C=O bridge to a cyclohexane-1,3-dione type ring, that is a benzoylcyclohexanedione
discrepancies.text_says: (57) Abstract, English: 'The invention relates to benzocyclohexandiones of general formula (I)'. Against that, (54) Title: 'BENZOYLCYCLOHEXANDIONES', (54) Bezeichnung: 'BENZOYLCYCLOHEXANDIONE', and (57) Zusammenfassung: 'Es werden Benzoylcyclohexandione ... beschrieben'.

discrepancies.what: The abstracts state that Y and Z are a monoatomic bridging element, and the drawing is consistent with this: Y and Z are each drawn as a single labelled ring position. Recorded as an agreement, not a conflict, so that the check is on record.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Y and Z each occupy one ring vertex of the left ring, with the bracket ( )v carrying the variable CH2 count
discrepancies.text_says: 'Y und Z für ein einatomiges Brückenelement' / 'Y and Z are a monoatomic bridging element'
